observations: A broad, roughly square head fills most of the frame, outlined in thick black lines, with two circular eyeglass frames drawn in overlapping blue, white, and pink loops sitting across the middle of the face.
Color is applied in flat, irregular patches—orange and red on the left cheek, yellow across the upper right, cyan and light blue across the background and lower face—with no blending between zones.
Dense scribble lines in cyan, magenta, yellow-green, and white radiate outward from the head into all four corners, crossing over the black outline and continuing beyond the figure's edge.
reading: The face holds the center with a frontal steadiness, while the scribbled lines around it refuse to stay still. Circular glasses anchor the middle of the image, their overlapping loops drawing the eye inward. The flat color patches—warm on the left cheek, cool across the background and lower face—read as a split rather than a unified surface. An open mouth with small zigzag marks inside adds a note of tension or animation to the otherwise planted composition.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between 'nnxyz nifty faces #3' and 'nnxyz nifty faces #5' in both title order and recorded creation order. Where #3 tilts off-axis into red and black, #4 plants itself squarely forward in cooler cyan tones. Title order and recorded creation order align here.

connections.reason: Both use a large black-outlined head with flat color patches and surrounding scribble lines, but #3 tilts off-axis and is dominated by red and magenta, while #4 faces forward with cyan and yellow as the dominant tones.

#5 builds a face entirely from dense looping lines with no flat color patches and no black outline, making it a direct contrast to #4's block-color-plus-outline approach despite sharing the same frontal head format.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the scribble lines cross over the black outline, and what happens to the sense of the figure's edge at those points?
ambiguities: The lettering in the lower right corner appears to read 'NA 2021' but functions here as signed content, not a confirmed date; software should validate.
The nnotb #5 comparison image shows heart forms and a warm red palette with no face-outline structure comparable to this work; no useful formal connection was found and it is excluded.
